name: Astronomy-Image-Captioning
description: The Astronomy-Image-Captioning dataset contains astronomical images paired with short captions, typically naming the celestial object or phenomenon shown. It evaluates a model's ability to generate accurate captions for space imagery.
card_text: The dataset consists of 200 image–text pairs focused on astronomy. Each sample provides a JPEG image of a celestial object (such as a galaxy, nebula, or star cluster) along with a text instruction and prompt asking the model to generate a caption. The target output is a concise caption, usually a factual title or descriptive name of the astronomical object (e.g., 'The Shape of the Southern Crab' or 'NGC 3314: When Galaxies Overlap'). The images vary in visual complexity, and the captions are short and encyclopedic in style. The task is open-set image captioning, requiring the model to recognize and describe astronomical content without a fixed label set. The dataset is designed to test visual recognition and captioning capabilities in the specialized domain of astronomy.

context.semantics: The task prompt instructs the model to analyze the accompanying astronomy image and generate a caption for it, establishing the captioning objective.

question.semantics: A direct instruction asking the model to generate a caption for the image, specifying the desired output.

image.semantics: Path to an astronomy image (e.g., a galaxy, nebula, or star cluster) that is the subject to be captioned.

answer.semantics: The target caption for the image, typically a short factual title or descriptive name of the astronomical object (e.g., 'NGC 3314: When Galaxies Overlap').

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample contains an astronomy image path (input.image_files), a task prompt (input.prompt), a direct instruction (input.instruction), and a target caption (output.caption). The image is the visual content to be described; the prompt and instruction ask the model to generate a caption for that image; the caption is a short factual title identifying the astronomical object. No additional context, rationale, options, or dialog fields are present.
